# AIMS64 handoff — input envelope + output contract (deck-design)

**Read this file when** the first non-blank block of the skill's input is a
YAML block containing `task_type: deck`. That marker means the skill is
being invoked by the AIMS64 platform's `orchestrator.md`, not by a human
user typing a natural-language brief.

In standalone mode (any input without that marker), ignore this file.

---

## Why this file exists

The skill behaves the same way in both modes — read the kit, map the
narrative to templates, materialise slides, verify — but the **input
shape** and **output shape** differ:

- **Standalone**: input is a free-form brief in chat; output is HTML
  slide files in `tmp/decks/<deck>/` plus a 5-line summary.
- **AIMS64 handoff**: input is a structured YAML envelope produced by
  `orchestrator.md`; output is a structured `deck_output` YAML the
  orchestrator can re-ingest for iteration / preview deployment.

This file documents only the handoff IO. Kit binding, composition rules,
and verification live in `kit-map.md`, `composition-rules.md`, and
`verification.md` — the same files used in standalone.

---

## Detecting handoff mode

The first non-blank block of input is YAML containing **at least** these
fields:

```yaml
task_type: deck
selected_design_systems:
  - dataart-corporate-uikit-v1
desired_outcome: files_only | preview_deploy | decide_later
```

If `task_type` is missing or differs from `deck`, this is not a deck
handoff — fall through to standalone mode.

> _Why a hard marker:_ without it, the skill cannot reliably distinguish
> "the user pasted a YAML draft of their deck" from "the orchestrator
> handed me an envelope". An explicit `task_type` is the contract.

---

## Input envelope — `skill_handoff` schema

```yaml
task_type: deck
selected_design_systems:
  - dataart-corporate-uikit-v1
approved_direction: string # one-sentence directive from human review
# desired_outcome — for decks, this is FIXED at `html_then_pptx` (or
# absent; both are treated identically). The deck pipeline is
# `HTML → preview → user OK → pptx via scripts/export-pptx.sh`. Any
# other value here is a malformed envelope and triggers an
# escalation_flag `malformed_envelope: desired_outcome must be
# html_then_pptx or absent`.
desired_outcome: html_then_pptx
deck_brief: # the narrative inputs
  title_hint: string | null
  angle: string # one-sentence thesis
  audience: string
  audience_knowledge: string
  emotional_target: string # what should they feel in the first 5 seconds
  belief_target: string # what should they believe by the last slide
  target_length: number | null # default 6-10 slides
  must_include: # required content beats
    - string
  must_avoid:
    - string
source_deck: # OPTIONAL — present only for a MIGRATION
  path: string # path to the source .pptx (or PDF)
  intent: preserve_structure # re-skin 1:1; keep content/order/count
# When `source_deck` is present, this is a MIGRATION envelope: switch to
# migration mode and follow `references/deck-migration.md` (ingest with
# scripts/extract-source-deck.py, preserve the source's slides, adapt design,
# offer the DataArt inserts once). The mandatory skeleton does NOT apply;
# `deck_brief` fields are advisory framing, not a rebuild spec.
# client_brand_overlay is OMITTED from deck handoff envelopes — decks
# are always rendered in canonical DataArt brand. If an envelope
# carries this field, raise `escalation_flag:
# brand_overlay_not_applicable_to_decks` and ignore.
#
# Figma URLs (when present) are conditional reference material; declare
# them here instead — non-empty enables figma-conditional.md.
figma_links:
  - url: string
    node_ids: [string]
iteration_context: # present only on refinement runs
  prior_run_id: string
  iteration_number: number
  prior_output: # previous deck_output for diffing
    <deck_output>
  feedback: string # human-review delta
required_context: # raw context the orchestrator mounted
  company_base: <yaml>
  deck_context: <yaml>
  workspace_context: <yaml>
optional_context:
  project_memory: <yaml>
```

### Validation rules

- `task_type: deck` — required.
- `selected_design_systems` — required; should contain
  `dataart-corporate-uikit-v1`. If it contains anything else, escalate:
  this skill binds only to the DataArt kit.
- `desired_outcome` — must be `html_then_pptx` or absent. Any other
  value (`files_only`, `preview_deploy`, `decide_later`) is treated as
  malformed and escalated; the deck pipeline cannot honour them.
- `deck_brief.angle` and `deck_brief.audience` — required (the
  narrative depends on them).

If a required field is missing, emit `deck_output` with `build_status:
failed` and a clear `escalation_flags` entry naming the missing field.

---

## Output contract — `deck_output`

Emit this exact YAML envelope on every handoff-mode run, even when the
build failed (in that case populate `escalation_flags` and leave
generation-only fields blank).

```yaml
deck_output:
  title: string
  angle: string # one-sentence thesis
  audience: string
  emotional_target: string
  belief_target: string
  narrative_summary: string # 3-5 lines describing the arc
  selected_design_system: dataart-corporate-uikit-v1
  kit_root: string # absolute path or <KIT_ROOT> placeholder
  ui_kit_paths_used:
    - <KIT_ROOT>/shared/tokens.css
    - <KIT_ROOT>/shared/layouts.css
    - <KIT_ROOT>/shared/components.css
    - <KIT_ROOT>/showcase/index.html
    - <KIT_ROOT>/templates/<list>
  deck_output_root: tmp/decks/<deck-name>/
  slides:
    - index: number
      file: tmp/decks/<deck-name>/slide-NN-<slug>.html
      template: cover | cover-2logo | section-divider | final | content-cards | content-table | content-timeline | content-pipeline | asis-fastfacts | … (any kit-corporate/templates/*.html stem)
      reuse_mode: reused | adapted | new-object
      role: string
      headline: string
      support_copy: string
      illustrations:
        - <KIT_ROOT>/assets/<file>
      background: bg-title-0N | bg-content-0N | bg-cover-light | none # the slide's chosen background (kit-map § 4)
      visual_notes: string
      weak_claim: true | false
  new_objects_introduced:
    - name: string
      slide_index: number
      purpose: string
      composed_from:
        - .layer
        - .txt-h9
        - var(--c-blue-400)
      reason_kit_insufficient: string
  # client_overlay_applied is OMITTED from deck_output — decks render
  # in canonical DataArt brand, never carry a client overlay (Part 13).
  verification:
    pixel_checks_passed: true | false
    console_clean: true | false
    notes:
      - string
  # Part 40: kit-resolution + self-check trace — REQUIRED before
  # output emission. Output is blocked when these fields are missing,
  # empty, or carry blocking_violations.
  kit_path_resolved:
    string # path captured in SKILL.md Step 0
    # (find-kit.sh output OR Read-tool
    # confirmation of three CSS files).
    # Two acceptable forms — record
    # which one was used:
    #   "<skill-dir>/kit-corporate/ (linked
    #     via ../../../)"
    #   "tmp/decks/<deck-name>/shared/
    #     (copied from bundled kit,
    #     self-contained — Cowork
    #     fallback)"
  self_check:
    ran_at: <ISO-8601>
    gates_checked:
      - name: kit_path_resolved # Step 0 — kit available
        passed: true | false
        evidence: string
      - name: kit_stylesheets_per_slide # all slides link 3 kit sheets
        passed: true | false
        evidence: string # e.g. "12 of 12 slides clean"
      - name: kit_substitution_check # § 6.7 — no CDN / non-kit / inline
        passed: true | false
        evidence: string # e.g. "0 substitutions detected"
      - name: rect_checks # existing position validation
        passed: true | false
        evidence: string
      - name: console_clean # existing 404 / JS errors
        passed: true | false
        evidence: string
      - name: composition_contrast # § 6.1-6.7 contrast gates
        passed: true | false
        evidence: string
      - name: l1_rhythm_check # Step 9a verify-deck.sh
        passed: true | false
        evidence: string
    pptx_export_method:
      native | deferred_to_claude_code | skipped_pending_install | not_requested
      # Part 41 + 54 — set by Step 11
      # path resolution. ONE working
      # path (Tier 1 via export-pptx.py).
      # When Cowork lacks the toolchain,
      # user picks: switch to Claude
      # Code (recommended), install in
      # Cowork once, or skip.
      #   native                   — scripts/export-pptx.py via
      #                              Playwright (pixel-perfect
      #                              editable text). Runs silently
      #                              if toolchain present. In
      #                              Cowork: works after the
      #                              .command installer ran once.
      #   deferred_to_claude_code  — User chose «open in Claude
      #                              Code» — HTML delivered,
      #                              pptx will be made there.
      #   skipped_pending_install  — User chose «skip pptx for
      #                              now» — HTML delivered;
      #                              installer remains in chat.
      #   not_requested            — Checkpoint #1 → «Skip pptx
      #                              (HTML only)» from the start.
    blocking_violations: # empty when ready to ship
      - gate: string
        fix_hint: string
    non_blocking_findings:
      - gate: string
        note: string
  # Pre-materialization plan (present when Checkpoint #0 fired — see
  # agent/references/execution-checkpoints.md).
  slide_plan:
    - idx: number
      slug: string
      template: string
      purpose: string
  # Checkpoint trail — always present. One entry per fired checkpoint.
  checkpoint_history:
    - checkpoint: 0 | 1
      decision: approved | modified | restarted | skipped | yes | changes_needed | discarded
      iterations: number
      notes: string | null
  # PPTX path — populated when Checkpoint #1 resolved to `Yes, export pptx`.
  # Null when `Skip pptx (HTML only)`. Decks never carry desired_outcome —
  # the pipeline is fixed at html_then_pptx.
  pptx_path: string | null
  build_status: success | failed | partial
  deploy_status: deployed | not_deployed | updated
  preview_url: string | null
  open_questions:
    - string
  human_refinement_needed:
    - string
  escalation_flags:
    - string
  iteration_context:
    prior_run_id: string | null
    iteration_number: number | null
    what_changed:
      - string
```

### Field rules

- `build_status` — required. `success` only when all slides materialised
  and the verification block returned `passed: true` for each. `partial`
  when some slides shipped but others failed verification. `failed` when
  no usable deck was produced.
- `deploy_status` — `not_deployed` unless `desired_outcome:
preview_deploy` was honoured. Never deploy silently.
- `verification.pixel_checks_passed` — required. Computed by running
  `scripts/verify-slide.sh` on every slide and aggregating the
  `passed` field. If any slide fails, this is `false` and the failing
  slides go into `verification.notes`.
- `new_objects_introduced` — keep ≤ 1 per ~5 slides on average; more is
  a design smell that should be flagged in `escalation_flags`.
- `iteration_context.what_changed` — required on iteration runs.
- `kit_path_resolved` (Part 40) — **required**. Output is blocked
  when this field is missing or empty. Captured in SKILL.md Step 0
  via `find-kit.sh` (bash) or via Read-tool probe on
  `kit-corporate/shared/tokens.css` etc. (Cowork / Claude.ai sandbox). A
  deck without a verified kit path is not a DataArt deck.
- `self_check` (Part 40) — **required**. Output is blocked when:
  - the block is missing entirely → emit
    `escalation_flag: self_check_trace_missing` + `build_status: failed`;
  - `gates_checked[]` is empty → same as missing;
  - `blocking_violations[]` is non-empty → fix the violation and
    re-run self-check before emitting files / preview / pptx.
    Receiving systems (orchestrator, human review, automated
    consumers) treat the absence of this trace as a process violation
    and reject the artefact. There is no path to ship a deck without
    it.

---

## Iteration handling

If the input envelope carries `iteration_context.prior_output`, treat
the run as refinement:

1. Diff `prior_output.slides` against the new plan; preserve approved
   slides and their templates.
2. Carry forward `prior_output.new_objects_introduced` entries that are
   still in use — do not regenerate from scratch.
3. Apply the human-review `feedback` field surgically.
4. Populate `iteration_context.what_changed` in the output with one
   sentence per delta (slide index, what changed, why).

---

## Escalation conventions

Single-sentence flags, machine-readable verb up front:

- `missing-required-field: deck_brief.angle`
- `non-default-design-system: <id>` (when `selected_design_systems`
  contains anything other than `dataart-corporate-uikit-v1`)
- `kit-not-found: scripts/find-kit.sh could not resolve <KIT_ROOT>`
- `figma-integration-missing: input includes figma_links but the Figma
MCP is not bound`
- `pixel-check-failed: slide-NN-<slug>.html, <which check>`
- `client-overlay-conflict: requested accent fails contrast`
- `runtime-preset-unsupported: preview_deploy requested but no preset`

`orchestrator.md` reads these by prefix and surfaces them in the next
human-review packet.

---

## What this file does **not** own

- Canonical pixel positions, colour tokens, typography classes,
  template list — `references/kit-map.md`.
- Composition rules, client overlay rules, anti-AI rules, motion rules
  — `references/composition-rules.md`.
- Pixel verification mechanics — `references/verification.md`.
- Path arithmetic for kit / output / scripts — `SKILL.md` Kit Binding
  section and `scripts/find-kit.sh`.

This file is only the **IO contract** between `orchestrator.md` and the
skill.
